pages.text: Two years more, and at last I understood the temper of that shard.$(br2)It recognises weather itself. Ring it with twelve cornerstones that stand for the four extremes of every world, and set water as a mirror - then the sky-gate may open by a hair's breadth.

pages.name: Climate Portal
pages.text: Carve a 4x4 base: fill the central 2x2 with source water, and the outer twelve cells need only be paved with four kinds of cornerstone, interleaved.$(br2)Bitter-cold stone - Ice, Packed Ice, Blue Ice, Snow Block;$(br2)Abyssal stone - Obsidian, Crying Obsidian;$(br2)Barren stone - Sand, Sandstone, Gravel;$(br2)Burning stone - Magma Block, Nether Bricks, Netherrack.$(br2)Any like material may be substituted freely - there is no need to hunt for rare Blue Ice or vanilla Obsidian.$(br2)(Click 'Visualize'; the 3D model cycles through every substitute material of each kind, once a second.)

pages.title: To Walk Into the Unknown
pages.text: When all was ready, I cast the $(item)Climate Shard$() into the heart of the pool.$(br2)In a moment, thunder fell from the sky and struck the water; the water became a gate, and beyond it, an endless blizzard and a howling wind.$(br2)I looked for a long while. Then I stepped through.$(br2)- If anyone reads this page, look for me: see whether there is, after all, a spring on the far side.
